y2turf 0.0.1
  • Reference

    y2turf

    Fast TURF (total unduplicated reach and frequency) analysis. turf() finds the combinations of products that reach the most respondents. It builds each combination in batches, refined with swap searches, rather than scoring every possible combination. The search is implemented in Rust via savvy.

    Installation

    Building from source requires a Rust toolchain (cargo and rustc). Install it from https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install, then:

    # install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Adam-Hubbs/y2turf")

    Usage

    Activation data has one row per respondent and one column per product, with 1 where a respondent is activated by a product and 0 otherwise. The package includes a simulated example, am.

    library(y2turf)

turf(
  am,
  possible_products = colnames(am),
  num_products = 4,
  batch_size = 2,
  keep_n_at_batch = 10,
  num_return = 3
)

    The result has one row per combination, best first, with its products, total_reach, and total_frequency. See ?turf for how the search works and how its arguments trade speed against thoroughness.

    Development

    The Rust source lives in src/rust/src/. R/000-wrappers.R, src/init.c, and src/rust/api.h are generated from it, so don’t edit them by hand.

    • After changing a #[savvy] function’s signature or docs, run savvy::savvy_update() to regenerate the bindings, then devtools::document().
    • Build only through R (devtools::document(), devtools::load_all(), devtools::install()), not bare cargo build, which lacks the environment R’s build tools provide. cargo clippy and cargo fmt are fine.
    • Builds always use the release profile, so timings reflect real performance. Set SAVVY_PROFILE=dev for a debug build.
    • To clean the build, delete src/rust/target. Don’t use devtools::clean_dll(): it deletes compiled files inside src/rust/target that cargo doesn’t know to rebuild, and the next build fails with “could not find native static library unwind_protect”. Deleting src/rust/target fixes it.
